title: Emergent low-energy many-body Hilbert spaces in Chern bands
authors: Chen-Xin Jiang, Zi-Xiang Hu, Bo Yang
abstract: We show that in Landau levels and more generic Chern bands, the most relevant many-body subspace selected by realistic two-body interactions alone (e.g., in the limit of vanishing bandwidth and band gap) depends strongly on the particle density and can be constructed systematically. Using the well-defined hierarchical structure of conformal Hilbert spaces (CHS), each with a highest-density vacuum state, we compute, for both fermionic and bosonic systems, the many-body quantum metric that quantifies the interaction energy scales of these subspaces. For a large family of short-range, Coulomb-based interactions, particles preferentially occupy the many-body states in the smallest accommodating CHS. This allows us to describe the low-energy physics of the interacting system in terms of the appropriate anyonic degrees of freedom. Our results also explain why, in any Chern band (in lattice or continuum systems), band mixing tends to be suppressed even in the limit of strong interaction; this suppression is stronger when the band deviates less from the ideal trace condition and when the two-body interaction is shorter-ranged.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework using Conformal Hilbert Spaces (CHS) to identify the low-energy subspace in strongly correlated systems like those found in Chern bands. By calculating a quantum metric, the authors show that interactions naturally select a specific, robust subspace, explaining phenomena like band polarization in Landau levels. This provides a systematic way to analyze complex interacting electron systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize the low-energy, physically relevant many-body subspace ($\bar{F}_s$) in strongly correlated quantum systems where the full Hilbert space is intractable.
main_result: The low-energy physics is governed by Conformal Hilbert Spaces (CHS), which naturally select the most relevant subspace based on particle density and interaction strength.
method: The authors systematically construct the relevant subspace using the framework of Conformal Hilbert Spaces (CHS) and compute the many-body quantum metric to quantify interaction energy scales.
model_or_system: The study focuses on systems exhibiting Chern bands, particularly Landau levels (LLs) and flat-band limits, applied to materials like twisted MoTe2 and magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (TBG).
key_observables: Many-body quantum metric ($\chi^{-1}$), band occupation fraction, and the many-body energy gap ($\Delta E$).
important_parameters: Particle density, interaction type (Coulomb, Yukawa), and the band gap ($\epsilon_g$), especially in the strong interaction limit.
main_assumptions: The low-energy physics is assumed to be governed by the CHS with the smallest vacuum filling factor greater than the actual filling factor.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate energy gaps and band occupation fractions for LLs, tMoTe2, and TBG across varying gap conditions, alongside detailed finite-size scaling plots for occupation and energy differences.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the problem in general Chern bands to applying the CHS formalism, calculating the quantum metric, and finally performing detailed finite-size scaling analyses on specific material models (LLs, tMoTe2, TBG) under various interaction strengths.
why_interesting: The use of the CHS framework provides a powerful, algebraic tool to predict the low-energy physics of interacting electrons in topological materials, which is highly relevant for understanding correlated topological phases.

FIG. 3. Schematic illustrations of the CHS hierarchy and flux insertion on a torus. (a) Schematic illustration of a representative CHS hierarchy for either fermionic or bosonic systems, with nested regions indicating subspace inclusion. The blue region represents how the many-body Hilbert space fills up when particles are added, mimicking a fuzzy many- body “Fermi surface” that is well defined for both interacting fermions and bosons. (b) Fluxes through the two noncon- tractible cycles of the torus define the twist angles θ and ϕ.
